hypothesis: With posterior-pole geometry fixed and each eye restricted to three discrete effective focal lengths, the object-side demand determines the source distance while focal length and pupil independently determine the source footprint bounds at the posterior pole.
limitations: The supplied presentation gives focal-length ranges, not three exact values; endpoints and arithmetic midpoint are used and remain configurable.
The model is a paraxial effective thin-eye model with a fixed posterior-pole plane, not a multi-surface anatomical eye.

A zero geometric minimum means the pupil footprint alone covers the target disk; it does not imply a physically zero-sized emitter, so the conservative full-overlap value is the recommended engineering bound.
Absolute irradiance and biological safety remain out of scope without measured radiometry, exposure, spectrum, and tissue transmission.
next_step: Replace the endpoint-plus-midpoint focal values if independently measured triplets become available, then add calibrated radiometry and a multi-surface non-sequential anatomical model.
objective: Correct the eye-illumination simulation so object-side requirements from 60 D to 120 D are evaluated by varying source distance while each eye uses only three fixed equivalent focal lengths and the posterior pole remains fixed.
observations: The complete matrix contains 252 eye-focal-pupil-demand cases and no accommodation output.
The conservative source diameter is always at least the geometric minimum; 54 cases have a zero geometric minimum because the pupil footprint already spans the target.
For the adult eye at 16.7 mm focal length and 5.0 mm pupil, the conservative diameter decreases from 10.388511 mm at 60 D to 7.694256 mm at 120 D.
The 600000-ray Monte Carlo comparison shows the geometric-minimum case captures all sampled rays but has lower uniformity, whereas the conservative case improves posterior-pole uniformity.
Six independently created OpticStudio systems agree with the analytical footprint bounds to within 2.5757174171303632e-11 micrometres.
